name_reason: Already compliant: data_fd2_<domain=dialog>_<descriptor=current_speaker_char_ptr>. Descriptor correctly reflects both role (current dialog speaker) and datatype (pointer to a character record). No Ghidra-address residue in the name. Domain 'dialog' is accurate since the value exists only to feed fd2_display_dialog_scene's portrait rendering.
purpose: Cached pointer to the current dialog speaker's character record, used by the dialog VM to fetch that speaker's portrait/position when rendering an in-dialog sprite.
logic_summary: Mutable BSS scalar (4 bytes) holding a pointer. Writer fd2_find_char_by_id_or_template (@0x12C60) clears it to NULL on entry, then while scanning the battle runtime_char array sets it to the matching runtime_char* (whether that slot is alive or dead); on a full battle miss it falls back to scanning the menu-party roster (stride 0x50) and stores the matched template* (last match wins). Readers in fd2_display_dialog_scene (@0x161A7 and @0x1628C, the -0x11/-0x12 sprite-load opcode handlers, taken only when the opcode's char_id != 0x27) dereference it as runtime_char* to read ->bPortrait_id (+7) and ->bPos_x/y (+0/+1) and drive fd2_load_dat_resource + fd2_play_dialog_open_animation. Always written before any read on every path, so the binary keeps it zero-init.
datatype: pointer (stored as undefined4 / uint32) to a runtime_char or a menu-party roster template (both share the leading bChar_id@+8 / bPos_x@+0 / bPos_y@+1 / bPortrait_id@+7 layout fields used here)
element_semantics: Single scalar pointer slot; NULL when no character matched the requested char_id, otherwise the address of the speaker's character record (runtime_char* on a battle id-hit, or a menu roster template* on the fallback path).
comment_original_issue: Source comment block at btl_turn.c:1036-1049 was accurate overall but mis-attributed the readers to dialog opcodes -0x13/-0x14 ('ally portrait'); the actual reads of this global (disasm 0x161A7 / 0x1628C) occur in the -0x11/-0x12 sprite-load handlers, guarded by char_id != 0x27, immediately after the fd2_find_char_by_id_or_template call. The -0x13/-0x14 handlers compute the char pointer directly from runtime_char_array[id*0x50] and never touch this global.
notes: BSS (.object2), zero-init, undefined4 len 4 confirmed via Ghidra listing. 6 xrefs total: 2 READ (fd2_display_dialog_scene 0x161A7/0x1628C), 4 in fd2_find_char_by_id_or_template (3 WRITE + 1 READ at the NULL-check). Game write-xrefs present => is_const=false. Ghidra data plate was empty (null) so a concise plate was created; src comment block is the precise source of truth and was corrected for the opcode mis-attribution. Source uses uint32 for the pointer (matches Ghidra undefined4); type not changed (out of scope for this stage).
